heading: AI Biotech Intelligence
subheading: AI-native drug discovery, computational biology & longevity capital
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Biotech carries binary clinical risk; AI-discovery names trade on platform narratives years ahead of any FDA approval.
footnote: Figures approximate, from public reporting as of Sep 28, 2026. Refreshed weekly (Mondays). Always confirm current prices/valuations independently.

kpis.sub: TEMPUS AI AGREES TO ACQUIRE PERSONALIS IN AN ALL-STOCK MRD DEAL
kpis.label: Tempus is buying the cancer-monitoring diagnostics company for roughly $1.5B in stock, adding minimal-residual-disease (MRD) testing onto its genomic-data platform the same week an analyst upgrade and an earnings beat landed together. The deal still needs to close, and none of it touches the unresolved Guardant litigation.

kpis.sub: ILLUMINA (ILMN) KEEPS RALLYING — GURUFOCUS NOW FLAGS IT ~105% ABOVE FAIR VALUE
kpis.label: Shares added another 7.45% on Sept 24, extending the post-S&P-500-inclusion run to a fresh high; GuruFocus's GF Value model puts fair value at $133.21 against a $273.90 price. The turnaround (FY2025 net income $850M, UBS's $260 target) is real, but the stock has now run past even the bulls, and a mechanical removal from Russell mid-cap indices this month is the same flow logic running in reverse.

kpis.sub: RECURSION LOCKS IN A DATED, THREE-YEAR REVENUE LINE WITH TEMPUS AI
kpis.label: Recursion extended its data-license deal with Tempus through November 2029 for $42M in committed fees, and granted Tempus a new non-exclusive global license to its RNA foundation model, TxFM. Shares rose about 2.6% on the Sept 24 news, part of a steadier climb from $3.40 (Aug 31) to roughly $3.89 — a platform's first quantifiable, multi-year revenue commitment rather than a discretionary collaboration.

kpis.sub: ARKG AUM CLIMBS BACK FROM $1.93B AS TOP-10 CONCENTRATION RISES TO 61.85%
kpis.label: Assets reversed their prior slide, recovering alongside the fund's own price highs; YTD total return has accelerated to roughly +85% and the trailing 12-month figure to roughly +98%. The fund's average annual return since its October 2014 inception is still only about 9.2% a year — a reminder of what “right eventually” has cost holders who didn't time the last two months.

themes.tag: A DATA-PLATFORM RALLY TURNS INTO AN ACQUISITION
themes.title: Tempus AI agrees to buy Personalis for ~$1.5B in stock, folding MRD testing into its genomic-data platform
themes.description: Tempus is using its own richly-valued stock as acquisition currency to add minimal-residual-disease cancer monitoring to its platform, announced the same week as an analyst upgrade and an earnings print that together fueled the stock's ~40% run the week prior. The deal adds integration and execution risk on top of a Guardant litigation overhang that hasn't moved, and it dilutes existing holders even as Tempus's Chief Accounting Officer sold $529,650 of stock on Sept 24 — ordinary 10b5-1 activity, but a data point worth noting alongside a stock-funded deal.

themes.tag: THE SAME STORY THAT JUSTIFIED THE INDEX ADD NOW READS AS A WARNING
themes.title: Illumina's rally outruns even its own bulls; GuruFocus flags shares roughly 105% over fair value
themes.description: The turnaround behind Illumina's S&P 500 return is real — FY2025 net income of $850M, seven analyst EPS raises in 60 days, a UBS target of $260 — but the stock closed at $273.90 this week, already above that bullish target and, per GuruFocus's GF Value model, roughly double its $133.21 fair-value estimate. A parallel removal from Russell mid-cap indices is the same mechanical flow working in reverse. Fundamentals and flows got Illumina here; from this price, flows are doing more of the work.

themes.tag: A COMPUTATIONAL-BIOLOGY PLATFORM BOOKS ITS FIRST REAL, DATED CONTRACT
themes.title: Recursion extends its Tempus AI data deal to $42M over three years and licenses out its RNA foundation model
themes.description: The extension, through November 2029, replaces discretionary payments with $42M of committed fees and grants Tempus a new non-exclusive, global license to Recursion's proprietary RNA foundation model, TxFM. It's a small number in isolation, but it's the platform's first quantifiable, multi-year revenue line tied to its own technology rather than a fee-for-service collaboration — the kind of proof point bulls have been waiting for since the Roche/Bayer/Merck/Sanofi/Genentech deals were signed.

themes.tag: FLOWS REVERSE, BUT THE MULTI-YEAR MATH DOESN'T CHANGE
themes.title: ARKG's AUM climbs back above $2B even as its 12-year annualized return sits near 9%
themes.description: Assets under management recovered from $1.93B to roughly $2.08B as Illumina and Tempus's rallies pulled the fund to fresh highs and pulled in some fresh money alongside them — a reversal of the redemptions-into-strength pattern flagged two weeks ago. Concentration keeps building anyway: the top 10 holdings are now 61.85% of the fund. None of this changes the fund's own 12-year track record: roughly 9.2% average annual return since its October 2014 inception, a fraction of what a plain S&P 500 index fund returned over the same stretch.

private_watchlist.name: Isomorphic Labs
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week. Still targeting first trials by year-end 2026 for ISM8969 (a year behind the original 2025 target); being Alphabet-owned makes a near-term IPO unlikely regardless of how the AI-pacing debate develops elsewhere.

private_watchlist.name: Insilico Medicine
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week. Rentosertib's Phase III (GENESIS-IPF) remains underway with a realistic approval window of 2029-2030 per the lead investigator's own estimate — years, not quarters, from here. Still the only name in this group already public (HKEX, Dec 2025, $292M IPO).

private_watchlist.name: Xaira Therapeutics
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week. The company continues hiring out its business-development function to line up partnerships that supply preclinical disease-area data rather than capital — it says the $1.3B already raised covers its near-term needs — but no partner has been named and no trial has started.

private_watchlist.name: NewLimit
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week. Still the year's largest single disclosed longevity round (~71% of 2026's disclosed longevity funding through August); its first candidate medicine remains in large-scale manufacturing with clinical entry targeted as early as 2027.

bear_case.title: Biology still fails in the clinic — and the clock hasn't moved
bear_case.description: Zero AI-discovered drugs have reached full FDA approval, out of 200+ now in clinical development. Insilico's own lead investigator still puts rentosertib's realistic timeline at 2029-2030, not the 2027-28 window discussed a year ago — a reminder that even the field's clearest proof point remains years away.

bear_case.title: Diagnostics litigation remains a three-way mess with no resolution in sight
bear_case.description: No movement this week on any of the three active fronts: Guardant's suit against Tempus (surviving dismissal since Aug 27), Tempus's dismissed-with-prejudice suit against Guardant (under appeal since Feb), or the $245.2M TwinStrand judgment against Guardant (also under appeal). Three lawsuits, two companies, years of legal spend ahead regardless of outcome — and now a $1.5B acquisition for Tempus to integrate on top of it.

bear_case.title: The two best 2026 stories on this page are now priced for perfection
bear_case.description: GuruFocus puts Illumina's fair value at $133.21 against a $273.90 close — roughly a 105% premium — and separately flags Schrödinger's own GF Score as overvalued after its ~60% one-month run. Both moves rest on real fundamental and platform progress, but the re-rating has now outrun the news in the two names carrying the largest stance weight on this page.

bear_case.title: M&A adds execution risk on top of binary clinical risk
bear_case.description: Tempus is funding its Personalis acquisition with richly-valued stock while still carrying an unresolved Guardant lawsuit and integrating a $1.5B deal into a company that only recently turned profitable. Roll-ups are a different risk profile than platform bets, and the market is currently pricing both the same way.

bear_case.title: The broader sector is running into its own rate wall heading into Q4
bear_case.description: Coverage this week frames XBI as hitting an "interest rate wall" with 40-plus named biotech catalysts still ahead before year-end — a crowded, priced-for-good-news setup that leaves little room for a single disappointing readout, and one where a hawkish Fed surprise would hit richly-valued platform names hardest.
